newsitem.title: USA: New Jersey lawmakers introduce spending plan.
newsitem.headline: New Jersey lawmakers introduce spending plan.

text.p: - New Jersey's spending plan for the fiscal year starting July 1 was introduced Thursday, although legislators did not wait to see it.
Key legislators and staffers worked all day on the final details of a $16.8-billion, election-year budget that has grown by $400 million since Gov Christine Whitman introduced it in January.

Among the new spending is $246 million to satisfy the state Supreme Court order to increase state aid to the 28 poorest school districts; $55 million in high-tech grants for higher education plus $30 million for college salaries, and $18 million to increase the state's child protection staff.
Two proposals were rejected -- $100 million to pay mostly urban hospitals for charity care and $55 million to fund a child-care tax credit.
The extra spending was made possible by two developments.
-- Whitman's plan to sell $2.75 billion in pension bonds, enabling the state to skip $590 million in contributions.
-- An unanticipated tax revenue windfall, estimated to exceed budget projections by $500 million.
Legislators will get their first look at the budget Monday, but in a year in which all 40 Senate seats and 80 in the Assembly will be on the November 4 ballot, little opposition is expected.
